overview: A consistent-hash LB routes all editors of a doc to one collaboration server which orders ops, transforms them (OT) and broadcasts; ops appended to a log, snapshots every N ops to object storage.

estimation.result: One document session must serialize or merge at least 100 operations/s.
estimation.implication: Shard by document rather than splitting one OT document across uncoordinated leaders.

components.rationale: Keep validation and durable state in services; retry only according to the API contract.

components.purpose: Routes by document id: all editors of a doc share one session server
components.rationale: Health checks and routing policy support scale-out; connection-based systems need compatible session routing.

components.purpose: Operational transform (OT) per document session; broadcasts ops, cursors and presence
components.rationale: Durable history is stored separately; shared routing/pub-sub connects clients on different gateway instances.

components.purpose: Store partitioned point-lookup state for google docs.
components.rationale: Define the partition key and consistency requirements; conditional writes protect version and ownership checks.

components.purpose: Snapshot every 500 ops; load = snapshot + tail of the op log
components.rationale: Publish metadata pointers only after objects are complete; use checksums, versioned keys and lifecycle cleanup.

components.purpose: Implement the owned APIs and coordinate state transitions for google docs.
components.rationale: Keep request handlers stateless where possible; the datastore or a fenced owner enforces concurrency invariants.

components.purpose: Store authoritative records with transactional constraints for google docs.
components.rationale: Choose keys and indexes from the documented access patterns; replicas provide availability, not conflict-free arbitrary writes.

accessPatterns: Append an acknowledged operation; load operations after a snapshot cursor.
constraints: Dedup operation_id; OT uses a document leader revision, CRDT uses stable actor/logical IDs.

entityDetails.purpose: Document metadata and the latest snapshot checkpoint.
accessPatterns: Check access before joining; retrieve a checkpoint on open.
constraints: Publish the snapshot and checkpoint together; retain operations newer than the checkpoint.

apiDetails.purpose: Join a document and exchange edits and ephemeral cursor presence.
apiDetails.rationale: Persist edits before ack. OT transforms against the server revision; CRDT exchanges state vectors and missing updates.

apiDetails.purpose: Open a document from a snapshot and the operation tail.
apiDetails.rationale: Authorize both snapshot access and log replay; a snapshot reduces startup replay work.

buildSteps.explanation: In Design, add Web Client and name it “Editor”. Place it in the leftmost caller/background lane. User-facing caller for google docs. steps.title: Editor → LB → Collaboration servers → Op log
steps.explanation: Route by document, validate the base revision, transform concurrent operations and persist the server-ordered edit before ack.

steps.title: Collaboration servers → Snapshots
steps.explanation: Periodically write a snapshot at a committed revision.

steps.title: Editor → LB → Docs API → Doc metadata
steps.explanation: Authorize the document and locate its current snapshot/checkpoint.

steps.title: Docs API → Snapshots
steps.explanation: Load a snapshot; the session replays the op-log tail. A failover needs a fenced document leader.

failureCases.scenario: Session server fails while editors are typing
failureCases.handling: Reconnect using the last durable revision/state vector and resend unacknowledged operation IDs. Rebuild from snapshot plus log; fence the old OT leader before admitting writes.

alternatives: Use a fenced OT document leader for a central revision order. Use CRDT updates for offline editing and multi-replica merging, budgeting identifier/tombstone overhead and safe compaction.
